doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

chapter: Opening and Kansas City head arrangements
title: The song 'Baby, meet me with your black drawers on'
summary: Monk Rowe opens the filming in San Diego and says the tune stuck in his head. The Cheathams say it came out as an unplanned head after the first album session.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: We are filming today in San Diego for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. And I’m really thrilled to have today as our guests, Jeannie and Jimmy Cheatham, masters of the blues, and educators. And I wanted to tell you something that happened to me on the way out here. Before I got on the plane in Syracuse I was listening to some of your records. So all the way on the plane, all seven hours, I had this, “Baby, meet me with your black drawers on.” That was in my head, all the way out here.
Imagine us doing that to ya.
And you know that’s the mark of a great tune.
If it sticks with you like that.
How did you guys come up with that?

It just sort of came out. You know we were working on that first album, and we were just fooling around, and when we went in the studio, it was after the session was over, then we just went into — there was no arrangement or anything. And so we never dreamed they would ever put it on the record.
